author: _achan96_
bio: Research Fellow @GovAIOrg | AI policy | PhD from @Mila_quebec | from 🇨🇦
text:
Could automating AI R&D radically accelerate AI progress in an “intelligence explosion”?

Preliminary evidence suggests that it could.

In a new paper with authors across academia, civil society, and frontier AI companies (including @dawnsongtweets @merettm @jackclarkSF @Yoshua_Bengio @geoffreyhinton ), we assess the evidence & offer policy recommendations 🧵

author: _achan96_
bio: Research Fellow @GovAIOrg | AI policy | PhD from @Mila_quebec | from 🇨🇦
text:
On current trends, it’s possible that AI research & development (R&D) will be fully automated within the next few years. We should take this seriously.

Although the existing evidence is preliminary and sometimes mixed, it suggests that this positive feedback loop could lead to an “intelligence explosion” that compresses years of AI progress into months or less.

author: _achan96_
bio: Research Fellow @GovAIOrg | AI policy | PhD from @Mila_quebec | from 🇨🇦
text:
An intelligence explosion could pose extreme risks to society, such as by eroding checks on power and making us lose control over powerful AI systems.

To prepare for this possibility, we recommend that policymakers—including heads of government—urgently prioritize

1) Obtaining visibility into AI R&D automation
2) Developing ways to steer and constrain an intelligence explosion
3) Preparing society for the impacts of an intelligence explosion
